title: Opera Omnia I (Delarue-Lommatzsch)
shelf_note: An 1834 Latin edition of Origen (the Lommatzsch reprint of the De la Rue text) sits correctly in the europeanlibraries collection.
structure_note: The running head reads 'ORIGENIS IN MATTHAEUM' (Matthew commentary, series §60), which is odd under a title of 'Vol. 1'. In the Lommatzsch edition the Matthew commentary falls in a later volume, and the published date of 1834 fits that. One leaf cannot confirm this. With printed_repeats of 620 out of 1081 numbered pages, page numbers repeat on most numbered leaves: either pagination restarts (several volumes or parts in one scan) or the OCR misreads page numbers. This page is an example of the second: <page-num>312 where the leaf prints 342. Also, structure.pages_translated = 0 while the pages_translated field says 1300 and this page has a translation, so the counter is unreliable (E2).

book_verdict: A clean 19th-century edition, correctly shelved. The OCR loses or garbles several line ends under the scan's right-edge shadow, misreads the page number and invents a catchword. The translation restores the garbled words sensibly ("forgets the things that are behind", "fittingly"). Only minor apparatus slips remain: a wrong footnote anchor and a mislabelled variant note. The 'Vol. 1' title on a Matthew-commentary leaf, together with the heavy page-number repeats, deserves a catalogue check.
